description: Verify that DUT with multiple network interfaces uses DHCP through each interface independently — DISCOVER#1 (DIface-0) and DISCOVER#2 (DIface-1) carry distinct chaddr values (RFC 2131 §3.6 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
RFC 2131 §3.6 says each network interface gets its own independent DHCP client. Sharing chaddr across interfaces would conflate two separate bindings on the server. This is the only multi-iface §4.7 case (Topology 2: dual-veth-pair); the harness uses SECOND_VETH = 1 + per-iface tc8-dut registry.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester brings DUT up on two interfaces (DIface-0 and DIface-1).
2. Each iface independently emits DHCPDISCOVER.
3. Observation:
   • DISCOVER on DIface-0 carries chaddr_0   ← key check 1
   • DISCOVER on DIface-1 carries chaddr_1
   • chaddr_0 ≠ chaddr_1   ← key check 2

[Pass condition]
Both DISCOVERs observed AND their chaddr values differ.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_d0_discover / Fail_no_d1_discover — DISCOVER missing on the corresponding iface
• Fail_chaddr_collision — DIface-0 and DIface-1 share the same chaddr

verdicts.Pass: Each DUT iface ran DHCP independently with distinct chaddr — normal
verdicts.Fail_chaddr_collision: DIface-0 and DIface-1 share the same chaddr
